description: 30 e-commerce sales examples generated from actual DB schema.

examples.prompt: Total revenue, order count, and average order value by country, ranked by revenue descending.
examples.expected_sql: WITH country_revenue AS (SELECT country, SUM(total_order_value) AS total_revenue, COUNT(order_id) AS order_count, AVG(total_order_value) AS avg_order_value FROM sales.sales_business_view GROUP BY country) SELECT country, total_revenue, order_count, avg_order_value FROM country_revenue ORDER BY total_revenue DESC

examples.prompt: Monthly revenue trend with month-over-month growth percentage.
examples.expected_sql:
WITH monthly_revenue AS (
      SELECT 
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) AS year,
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) AS month,
        SUM(total_order_value) AS revenue
      FROM 
        sales.fact_orders
      GROUP BY 
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date),
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date)
    )
    SELECT 
      year,
      month,
      revenue,
      LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year, month) AS prev_revenue,
      ROUND(((revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year, month)) / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year, month)) * 100, 2) AS mom_growth
    FROM 
      monthly_revenue
    ORDER BY 
      year, month

examples.prompt: Order status distribution: count and percentage of total for each status.
examples.expected_sql:
WITH order_status_distribution AS (
      SELECT 
        order_status,
        COUNT(*) AS count
      FROM 
        sales.fact_orders
      WHERE 
        domain IN ('United States', 'United Kingdom')
      GROUP BY 
        order_status
    )
    SELECT 
      order_status,
      count,
      ROUND(count * 100.0 / SUM(count) OVER (), 2) AS percentage
    FROM 
      order_status_distribution
    ORDER BY 
      count DESC;

examples.prompt: Top 5 product categories by total revenue and profit.
examples.expected_sql:
WITH revenue AS (
      SELECT 
        dp.category,
        SUM(foi.total_price_usd) AS total_revenue,
        SUM(foi.total_price_usd - (foi.total_price_usd * (1 - foi.profit_margin_percent / 100))) AS total_profit
      FROM 
        sales.fact_order_items foi
      JOIN 
        sales.dim_product dp ON foi.product_id = dp.product_id
      GROUP BY 
        dp.category
    )
    SELECT 
      category,
      total_revenue,
      total_profit
    FROM 
      revenue
    ORDER BY 
      total_revenue DESC
    LIMIT 5;

examples.prompt: Delivery status breakdown by shipping method: count and average delivery days.
examples.expected_sql: WITH delivery_status AS ( SELECT delivery_status, delivery_days, CASE WHEN shipping_cost_usd > 0 THEN 'paid' WHEN shipping_cost_usd = 0 THEN 'free' END AS shipping_method FROM sales.fact_order_items ) SELECT shipping_method, delivery_status, COUNT(*) AS count, AVG(delivery_days) AS avg_delivery_days FROM delivery_status GROUP BY shipping_method, delivery_status ORDER BY shipping_method, delivery_status

examples.prompt: Weekend versus weekday order count and revenue comparison.
examples.expected_sql:
WITH weekend_orders AS (
      SELECT 
        COUNT(*) AS order_count,
        SUM(total_order_value) AS total_revenue
      FROM 
        sales.fact_orders fo
      JOIN 
        sales.dim_date dd ON fo.order_date::DATE = dd.order_date
      WHERE 
        dd.is_weekend = 'Yes'
    ),
    weekday_orders AS (
      SELECT 
        COUNT(*) AS order_count,
        SUM(total_order_value) AS total_revenue
      FROM 
        sales.fact_orders fo
      JOIN 
        sales.dim_date dd ON fo.order_date::DATE = dd.order_date
      WHERE 
        dd.is_weekend = 'No'
    )
    SELECT 
      'Weekend' AS order_type,
      wo.order_count,
      wo.total_revenue
    FROM 
      weekend_orders wo
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
      'Weekday' AS order_type,
      wd.order_count,
      wd.total_revenue
    FROM 
      weekday_orders wd

examples.prompt: Top 10 products by units sold and total revenue.
examples.expected_sql:
WITH product_sales AS (
      SELECT 
        p.product_name, 
        SUM(foi.quantity) AS total_units_sold, 
        SUM(foi.total_price_usd) AS total_revenue
      FROM 
        sales.fact_order_items foi
      JOIN 
        sales.dim_product p ON foi.product_id = p.product_id
      JOIN 
        sales.dim_customer c ON foi.customer_id = c.customer_id
      WHERE 
        c.country = 'United States'
      GROUP BY 
        p.product_name
    )
    SELECT 
      product_name, 
      total_units_sold, 
      total_revenue
    FROM 
      product_sales
    ORDER BY 
      total_units_sold DESC, 
      total_revenue DESC
    LIMIT 10;

examples.prompt: Customer age group analysis: bucket ages into decades and show order count and average order value per group.
examples.expected_sql:
WITH customer_age_groups AS (
      SELECT 
        CASE 
          WHEN age BETWEEN 0 AND 9 THEN '0-9'
          WHEN age BETWEEN 10 AND 19 THEN '10-19'
          WHEN age BETWEEN 20 AND 29 THEN '20-29'
          WHEN age BETWEEN 30 AND 39 THEN '30-39'
          WHEN age BETWEEN 40 AND 49 THEN '40-49'
          WHEN age BETWEEN 50 AND 59 THEN '50-59'
          WHEN age BETWEEN 60 AND 69 THEN '60-69'
          WHEN age BETWEEN 70 AND 79 THEN '70-79'
          WHEN age BETWEEN 80 AND 89 THEN '80-89'
          WHEN age BETWEEN 90 AND 99 THEN '90-99'
          ELSE '100+'
        END AS age_group,
        c.customer_id
      FROM sales.dim_customer c
    ),
    order_data AS (
      SELECT 
        cag.age_group,
        COUNT(foi.order_id) AS order_count,
        AVG(foi.total_price_usd) AS average_order_value
      FROM sales.fact_order_items foi
      JOIN customer_age_groups cag ON foi.customer_id = cag.customer_id
      GROUP BY cag.age_group
    )
    SELECT 
      age_group,
      order_count,
      average_order_value
    FROM order_data
    ORDER BY age_group;

examples.prompt: Coupon usage analysis: compare average order value, revenue, and order count for orders with and without coupon.
examples.expected_sql:
WITH coupon_orders AS (
      SELECT 
        SUM(total_order_value) AS revenue,
        AVG(total_order_value) AS avg_order_value,
        COUNT(order_id) AS order_count
      FROM 
        sales.sales_business_view 
      WHERE 
        coupon_used = 'Yes'
    ),
    non_coupon_orders AS (
      SELECT 
        SUM(total_order_value) AS revenue,
        AVG(total_order_value) AS avg_order_value,
        COUNT(order_id) AS order_count
      FROM 
        sales.sales_business_view 
      WHERE 
        coupon_used = 'No'
    )
    SELECT 
      'With Coupon' AS coupon_status,
      (SELECT revenue FROM coupon_orders) AS revenue,
      (SELECT avg_order_value FROM coupon_orders) AS avg_order_value,
      (SELECT order_count FROM coupon_orders) AS order_count
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
      'Without Coupon' AS coupon_status,
      (SELECT revenue FROM non_coupon_orders) AS revenue,
      (SELECT avg_order_value FROM non_coupon_orders) AS avg_order_value,
      (SELECT order_count FROM non_coupon_orders) AS order_count

examples.prompt: Customer loyalty score bands (0-2, 2-4, 4-6, 6-8, 8-10) versus average order value and total orders.
examples.expected_sql:
WITH loyalty_bands AS (
      SELECT 
        customer_id,
        CASE 
          WHEN customer_loyalty_score BETWEEN 0 AND 2 THEN '0-2'
          WHEN customer_loyalty_score BETWEEN 2 AND 4 THEN '2-4'
          WHEN customer_loyalty_score BETWEEN 4 AND 6 THEN '4-6'
          WHEN customer_loyalty_score BETWEEN 6 AND 8 THEN '6-8'
          WHEN customer_loyalty_score BETWEEN 8 AND 10 THEN '8-10'
        END AS loyalty_band
      FROM sales.dim_customer
    ),
    order_values AS (
      SELECT 
        customer_id,
        AVG(total_order_value) AS avg_order_value,
        COUNT(order_id) AS total_orders
      FROM sales.fact_orders
      GROUP BY customer_id
    )
    SELECT 
      lb.loyalty_band,
      AVG(ov.avg_order_value) AS avg_order_value,
      SUM(ov.total_orders) AS total_orders
    FROM loyalty_bands lb
    JOIN order_values ov ON lb.customer_id = ov.customer_id
    GROUP BY lb.loyalty_band
    ORDER BY lb.loyalty_band;

examples.prompt: Fraud risk score distribution: count of orders in low (0-0.3), medium (0.3-0.7), high (0.7-1.0) risk bands by country.
examples.expected_sql:
WITH risk_bands AS (
      SELECT 
        country,
        CASE 
          WHEN fraud_risk_score BETWEEN 0 AND 0.3 THEN 'Low'
          WHEN fraud_risk_score BETWEEN 0.3 AND 0.7 THEN 'Medium'
          WHEN fraud_risk_score BETWEEN 0.7 AND 1.0 THEN 'High'
        END AS risk_band
      FROM sales.fact_order_items
      WHERE country IN ('United States', 'Germany', 'France')
    )
    SELECT 
      country,
      SUM(CASE WHEN risk_band = 'Low' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS low_risk_count,
      SUM(CASE WHEN risk_band = 'Medium' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS medium_risk_count,
      SUM(CASE WHEN risk_band = 'High' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_risk_count
    FROM risk_bands
    GROUP BY country

examples.prompt: Year-over-year revenue comparison by month across all years in the data.
examples.expected_sql:
WITH monthly_revenue AS (
      SELECT 
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) AS order_year,
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) AS order_month,
        SUM(total_order_value) AS total_revenue
      FROM 
        sales.fact_orders
      GROUP BY 
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date),
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date)
    )
    SELECT 
      order_month,
      order_year,
      total_revenue,
      LAG(total_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY order_month ORDER BY order_year) AS prev_year_revenue,
      total_revenue - LAG(total_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY order_month ORDER BY order_year) AS revenue_diff
    FROM 
      monthly_revenue
    ORDER BY 
      order_month,
      order_year

examples.prompt: Sub-category profitability: revenue, profit, and profit margin percentage ranked by margin descending.
examples.expected_sql:
WITH sub_category_profit AS (
      SELECT 
        dp.sub_category,
        SUM(foi.total_price_usd) AS revenue,
        SUM(foi.profit_usd) AS profit,
        SUM(foi.profit_usd) / SUM(foi.total_price_usd) * 100 AS profit_margin_percent
      FROM 
        sales.fact_order_items foi
      JOIN 
        sales.dim_product dp ON foi.product_id = dp.product_id
      GROUP BY 
        dp.sub_category
    )
    SELECT 
      sub_category,
      revenue,
      profit,
      profit_margin_percent
    FROM 
      sub_category_profit
    ORDER BY 
      profit_margin_percent DESC;

examples.prompt: Installment plan usage: order count and average order value for orders using installments versus not.
examples.expected_sql:
WITH installment_orders AS (
      SELECT 
        CASE 
          WHEN dp.installment_plan IS NOT NULL AND dp.installment_plan <> '' THEN 'With Installment'
          ELSE 'Without Installment'
        END AS installment_usage,
        fo.order_id,
        fo.total_order_value
      FROM 
        sales.fact_orders fo
      LEFT JOIN 
        sales.dim_payment dp ON fo.payment_method = dp.payment_method AND fo.payment_status = dp.payment_status
    )
    SELECT 
      installment_usage,
      COUNT(order_id) AS order_count,
      AVG(total_order_value) AS avg_order_value
    FROM 
      installment_orders
    GROUP BY 
      installment_usage

examples.prompt: High value orders (above overall average order value): count and total revenue by customer segment and country.
examples.expected_sql:
WITH high_value_orders AS (
      SELECT 
        c.customer_segment,
        c.country,
        fo.total_order_value
      FROM 
        sales.dim_customer c
      JOIN 
        sales.fact_orders fo ON c.customer_id = fo.customer_id
      WHERE 
        c.customer_segment IN ('Premium', 'Regular')
        AND fo.total_order_value > (SELECT AVG(total_order_value) FROM sales.fact_orders)
    )
    SELECT 
      customer_segment,
      country,
      COUNT(*) AS count,
      SUM(total_order_value) AS total_revenue
    FROM 
      high_value_orders
    GROUP BY 
      customer_segment,
      country
    ORDER BY 
      customer_segment,
      country;

examples.prompt: Shipping cost as percentage of order value by shipping method.
examples.expected_sql: WITH orders AS (SELECT order_id, SUM(total_price_usd) AS order_value FROM sales.fact_order_items GROUP BY order_id), shipping_costs AS (SELECT order_id, shipping_cost_usd, delivery_status FROM sales.fact_order_items) SELECT delivery_status, AVG(shipping_cost_usd / order_value * 100) AS shipping_cost_percentage FROM shipping_costs JOIN orders USING (order_id) GROUP BY delivery_status

examples.prompt: Repeat versus one-time buyer analysis: count, total revenue, and average order value for each group.
examples.expected_sql:
WITH repeat_buyers AS (
      SELECT customer_id
      FROM sales.fact_orders
      GROUP BY customer_id
      HAVING COUNT(order_id) > 1
    ),
    one_time_buyers AS (
      SELECT customer_id
      FROM sales.fact_orders
      GROUP BY customer_id
      HAVING COUNT(order_id) = 1
    )
    SELECT 
      'Repeat' AS buyer_type,
      COUNT(DISTINCT fo.customer_id) AS count,
      SUM(fo.total_order_value) AS total_revenue,
      AVG(fo.total_order_value) AS average_order_value
    FROM sales.fact_orders fo
    WHERE fo.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM repeat_buyers)
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
      'One-time' AS buyer_type,
      COUNT(DISTINCT fo.customer_id) AS count,
      SUM(fo.total_order_value) AS total_revenue,
      AVG(fo.total_order_value) AS average_order_value
    FROM sales.fact_orders fo
    WHERE fo.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM one_time_buyers)

examples.prompt: Order priority distribution and average delivery days per priority level.

examples.prompt: Monthly unique active customers trend with month-over-month change.
examples.expected_sql:
WITH monthly_active_customers AS (
      SELECT 
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM fo.order_date) AS year,
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM fo.order_date) AS month,
        COUNT(DISTINCT fo.customer_id) AS unique_active_customers
      FROM 
        sales.fact_orders fo
      GROUP BY 
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM fo.order_date),
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM fo.order_date)
    ),
    monthly_change AS (
      SELECT 
        year,
        month,
        unique_active_customers,
        LAG(unique_active_customers) OVER (ORDER BY year, month) AS prev_month_customers
      FROM 
        monthly_active_customers
    )
    SELECT 
      year,
      month,
      unique_active_customers,
      unique_active_customers - prev_month_customers AS month_over_month_change
    FROM 
      monthly_change
    ORDER BY 
      year, month
